title: Find orders by comparing initial rates
body: To find the order with respect to each reactant, compare the initial rates of experiments and see how the rate changes when that reactant's concentration changes.
ced_evidence: 5.2.A.5 "Comparing initial rates of a reaction is a method to determine the order with respect to each reactant"

title: Requirements for a successful collision
body: Only a small fraction of collisions lead to reaction; a successful collision must meet both requirements below.

items.label: Sufficient energy
items.meaning: The colliding particles have enough energy to overcome the activation energy requirement.

items.label: Proper orientation
items.meaning: The particles collide in an orientation that allows the bonds to rearrange in the required manner.

ced_evidence: 5.5.A.2 "sufficient energy to overcome the activation energy requirements and orientations that allow the bonds to rearrange"

title: Maxwell-Boltzmann energy distribution
body: A curve of the distribution of particle energies, used qualitatively to estimate the fraction of collisions with enough energy to react and how that fraction depends on temperature.

items.label: Vertical axis
items.meaning: Number (or fraction) of particles at each energy.

items.label: Activation energy marker
items.meaning: The energy a collision needs in order to lead to a reaction.

items.label: Area beyond the activation energy
items.meaning: Qualitative estimate of the fraction of collisions with sufficient energy to react.

items.label: Effect of temperature
items.meaning: The fraction of collisions with sufficient energy depends on temperature (higher temperature puts a larger fraction beyond the activation energy).

ced_evidence: 5.5.A.3 "Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution curve describes the distribution of particle energies"

title: Reaction intermediate
body: A species produced by some elementary steps and consumed by others, so that it is present only while a reaction is occurring.
ced_evidence: 5.7.A.3 "produced by some elementary steps and consumed by others"

title: Types of catalysis named in the CED
body: Three catalytic pathways named in the CED, each introducing new reaction intermediate(s) and elementary reactions.

items.label: Binding to reactants (e.g., many enzymes)
items.meaning: The catalyst binds the reactant(s); they are oriented more favorably or react with lower activation energy, often forming a new intermediate with the catalyst bound.

items.label: Acid-base catalysis
items.meaning: Covalent bonding between catalyst and reactant(s); a reactant or intermediate gains or loses a proton, introducing a new intermediate and new elementary reactions.

items.label: Surface catalysis
items.meaning: A reactant or intermediate binds to, or forms a covalent bond with, the surface, introducing elementary reactions involving new bound intermediate(s).
